Definition: from G303 and G2212; to search out:--seek.
BiblicalUsage: Mary and Joseph search for the boy Jesus among their company on the road home from Jerusalem, and Barnabas goes to Tarsus to seek out Saul and bring him to Antioch. The word is a thorough searching, looking until the one sought is found.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for searching out holds no doctrine of its own; its charm is the picture, of parents hunting for their child and a friend hunting for a man the church needed.
RelatedPeople: Mary, Mother of Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary; Barnabas; Paul
RelatedEvents: The Boy Jesus in the Temple; The Church at Antioch
